expectedText:
EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Alex Lee · Acme Corp

ABOUT THIS EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN INFORMATION SHEET
This Emergency Action Plan Information Sheet describes California's Cal/OSHA regulation requiring most employers to establish an emergency action plan covering fire and other workplace emergencies, 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220, as that regulation relates to the working relationship between Jordan Alex Lee and Acme Corp.

It summarizes selected requirements of that regulation: what the plan must cover and when it must be written, the six elements the regulation itself requires the plan to include, the employee alarm system and evacuation-type requirements, when the employer must designate and train evacuation personnel, when and how employees must be advised of their responsibilities under the plan, and where the written plan must be kept, including the regulation's own exception for employers with 10 or fewer employees.

Acme Corp has identified Taylor Morgan as the person or department who can be contacted for further information or an explanation of duties under its plan.

This information sheet is not itself Acme Corp's emergency action plan, does not itself satisfy 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220's plan requirement, and does not determine that any particular practice of Acme Corp's is or is not compliant with California law.

SCOPE AND THE WRITTEN-PLAN REQUIREMENT
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(a) itself states that the section applies to all emergency action plans, that the plan shall cover those designated actions employers and employees must take to ensure employee safety from fire and other emergencies, and that the plan shall be in writing except as provided in the last sentence of subsection (e)(3) of the same section. That last sentence, addressed in a companion clause of this information sheet, is the regulation's own exception for employers with 10 or fewer employees.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(a) Scope and Application. This section applies to all emergency action plans. The emergency action plan shall be in writing, except as provided in the last sentence of subsection (e)(3) of this section, and shall cover those designated actions employers and employees must take to ensure employee safety from fire and other emergencies."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (a) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  Known gap: The regulation's own text does not itself state which employers are covered — it says the section 'applies to all emergency action plans' without separately defining which workplaces or industries must have one, or listing any industry-specific exemption from the underlying duty to have a plan at all (as distinct from the small-employer exception to the writing requirement, which is stated and is addressed separately). This document did not independently verify whether any other Title 8 provision narrows or exempts particular categories of employers from § 3220 itself; none was found in the text quoted here or elsewhere in this section. The quotation is drawn from a single subdivision of one regulation and is not corroborated by any second, independent source.

THE SIX ELEMENTS THE PLAN MUST INCLUDE
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(b) itself states that, at a minimum, six elements shall be included in the plan: procedures for emergency evacuation, including the type of evacuation and exit route assignments; procedures to be followed by employees who remain to operate critical plant operations before they evacuate; procedures to account for all employees after emergency evacuation has been completed; procedures to be followed by employees performing rescue or medical duties; the preferred means of reporting fires and other emergencies; and the names or regular job titles of persons or departments who can be contacted for further information or explanation of duties under the plan. Acme Corp has identified Taylor Morgan as the person or department who can be contacted for that purpose.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(b) Elements. The following elements, at a minimum, shall be included in the plan:"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (b) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(1) Procedures for emergency evacuation, including type of evacuation and exit route assignments;"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (b)(1) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(2) Procedures to be followed by employees who remain to operate critical plant operations before they evacuate;"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (b)(2) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(3) Procedures to account for all employees after emergency evacuation has been completed;"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (b)(3) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(4) Procedures to be followed by employees performing rescue or medical duties;"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (b)(4) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(5) The preferred means of reporting fires and other emergencies; and"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (b)(5) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(6) Names or regular job titles of persons or departments who can be contacted for further information or explanation of duties under the plan."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (b)(6) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  Known gap: The regulation's own phrase — 'at a minimum' — means the six listed elements are a floor, not a ceiling; the text quoted here does not itself state what, if anything, beyond these six elements a particular plan must contain. All six citations below are drawn from the same regulation, 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(b), and its numbered subparagraphs (1) through (6) — they are not independent sources of one another. This document did not independently verify the 2017 regulatory history note appearing on the source page, which states that subsections (b)(1) and (b)(4) were amended effective June 5, 2017; that amendment is not itself quoted or analyzed here, only the current text as fetched.

THE EMPLOYEE ALARM SYSTEM REQUIREMENT
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(c) itself requires the employer to establish an employee alarm system that complies with Article 165 of Title 8, and, if that alarm system is used for alerting fire brigade members or for other purposes in addition to signaling an emergency evacuation, it requires a distinctive signal to be used for each separate purpose.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(1) The employer shall establish an employee alarm system which complies with Article 165."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (c)(1) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(2) If the employee alarm system is used for alerting fire brigade members, or for other purposes, a distinctive signal for each purpose shall be used."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (c)(2) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  Known gap: This clause does not independently verify the content of Article 165 itself, the separate Title 8 employee-alarm-system standard that § 3220(c)(1) cross-references — that article was not fetched or quoted in this information sheet, so no claim is made here about what Article 165 itself requires of an alarm system beyond the requirement to comply with it. Both quotations in this clause are drawn from subdivisions (c)(1) and (c)(2) of the same regulation, 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220, not from two independent sources.

ESTABLISHING THE TYPES OF EVACUATION
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(d) itself requires the employer to establish, within the emergency action plan, the types of evacuation to be used in emergency circumstances.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(d) Evacuation. The employer shall establish in the emergency action plan the types of evacuation to be used in emergency circumstances."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (d) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  Known gap: The regulation's own text does not itself list or define what the available 'types of evacuation' are — it requires only that the plan establish which types apply, without naming categories (such as full-building evacuation versus a partial or phased evacuation) in the text quoted here. This is a single subdivision of one regulation, not corroborated by any second, independent source in this clause.

DESIGNATING AND TRAINING EVACUATION PERSONNEL
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(e)(1) itself requires that, before implementing the emergency action plan, the employer designate and train a sufficient number of persons to assist in the safe and orderly emergency evacuation of employees.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(1) Before implementing the emergency action plan, the employer shall designate and train a sufficient number of persons to assist in the safe and orderly emergency evacuation of employees."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (e)(1) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  Known gap: The regulation's own text does not itself state a numeric ratio, ratio of designated persons to total employees, or specific training curriculum — it requires only a 'sufficient number' of trained persons, a standard the text quoted here does not further define. This clause quotes a single subdivision of one regulation; the training obligations described in the companion clause of this information sheet covering subdivision (e)(2) are a separate requirement of the same subdivision (e), not an independent source.

WHEN EMPLOYEES MUST BE ADVISED OF THEIR RESPONSIBILITIES
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(e)(2) itself requires the employer to advise each employee of his or her responsibility under the plan at three specified times: initially when the plan is developed; whenever the employee's responsibilities or designated actions under the plan change; and whenever the plan itself is changed.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(2) The employer shall advise each employee of his/her responsibility under the plan at the following times:"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (e)(2) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(A) Initially when the plan is developed,"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (e)(2)(A) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(B) Whenever the employee's responsibilities or designated actions under the plan change, and"
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (e)(2)(B) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  "(C) Whenever the plan is changed."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (e)(2)(C) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  Known gap: The regulation's own text does not itself specify a method of notice (written memo, posted notice, verbal briefing, or otherwise) for advising employees at these three times, nor does it state a deadline measured in days after a change to the plan or to an employee's responsibilities. All three quotations in this clause — subparagraphs (A), (B), and (C) — are part of the same subdivision, 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(e)(2), and are not independent of one another or of the other clauses of this information sheet that also cite this regulation.

PLAN AVAILABILITY AND THE SMALL-EMPLOYER EXCEPTION
8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(e)(3) itself requires the employer to review with each employee, upon initial assignment, those parts of the plan the employee must know to protect the employee in the event of an emergency, and it requires that the written plan be kept at the workplace and made available for employee review. The same subdivision then states the exception that subdivision (a) cross-references for the writing requirement: for employers with 10 or fewer employees, the plan may be communicated orally to employees, and the employer need not maintain a written plan.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(3) The employer shall review with each employee upon initial assignment those parts of the plan which the employee must know to protect the employee in the event of an emergency. The written plan shall be kept at the workplace and made available for employee review. For those employers with 10 or fewer employees the plan may be communicated orally to employees and the employer need not maintain a written plan."
  — 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220 (California Department of Industrial Relations, Title 8 text), Cal. Code Regs., tit. 8, § 3220, subd. (e)(3) (https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3220.html)
  Known gap: The regulation's own text does not itself state whether the 10-or-fewer-employee count is measured company-wide, per worksite, or in some other way — the phrase quoted here is 'employers with 10 or fewer employees,' without further definition of how that number is calculated. This clause quotes a single subdivision, 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 3220(e)(3); it is the same subdivision that subdivision (a), addressed in a companion clause of this information sheet, cross-references as the source of the writing exception, so the two clauses describe the same regulatory text from two subdivisions of one section rather than from independent sources.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF RECEIPT
Please sign below to acknowledge that you received this Emergency Action Plan Information Sheet.

Employee: Jordan Alex Lee
Signature: _______________  Date: _______________

Contact for questions about the plan: Taylor Morgan
Signature: _______________  Date: _______________

On behalf of Acme Corp:
Signature: _______________  Date: _______________
